_readme: What Andhra Pradesh spent on school education, what it built, and what reached the schools, government by government since 2014. Spending is the Demands for Grants series, which is the state's voted budget and the measure the CAG audits. School and enrolment counts are UDISE+, the Ministry of Education's national census. Components are read from the state's own Government Orders. Per-student figures are OUR division of two published government figures and are labelled as such everywhere they appear. Government Order rupee amounts are NEVER summed as spending - see reconciliation.

tenures.label: Before the first post-bifurcation government
tenures.note: Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated on 2 June 2014 and the first government of the residuary state took office on 8 June. Orders on or before 7 June belong to no elected government of the present state.

spending.what_it_is: Demand XII, School Education, as voted and as audited. BE is the budget estimate, RE the revised estimate, Actual the audited outturn. Totals include salaries and running costs as well as construction, which is what 'spending on school education' normally means.

caveats.title: The auditor says part of the school capital spike was not capital at all
caveats.body: The Comptroller and Auditor General examined Mana Badi Nadu Nedu Phase I and found that spending on repairs, painting, desks and fans, which is running cost rather than asset creation, was booked as capital expenditure. That inflates the capital outlay column in exactly the years the programme ran. The jump is real and large, but a reader should know that some of it is an accounting choice the auditor objected to.
caveats.quote: MBNN Phase I involved repairs, painting, procurement of Desks, fans... the entire expenditure was booked under Capital Expenditure instead of Revenue Expenditure.
caveats.source_publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India, Report No. 5 of 2025, Chapter III

caveats.title: The first three years cannot be split into revenue and capital
caveats.body: Until 2017-18 the budget was presented as Plan against Non-Plan rather than revenue against capital. The demand totals for those years are on record and shown, but no capital outlay figure exists to extract from them. That is a change in how the state kept its books, not a gap in ours.
caveats.source_publisher: AP Finance Department, Statement of Demands for Grants

caveats.title: The 2022-23 cell that was blank, now filled — and the strange recovery behind it
caveats.body: The audited actual for School Education capital in 2022-23 is Rs 478.92 crore gross. We first left this cell blank because two reads of the same page produced two different figures, one negative. On 27 August 2026 we eye-checked the printed page of the 2024-25 volume: both figures are real. The page shows gross capital of Rs 478.92 crore, then deducts recoveries of Rs 501.58 crore — more than the entire year's outlay — leaving NET capital of MINUS Rs 22.66 crore. The volume does not say what was recovered or why. We show the gross figure in the series, because every other year in the series is gross, and we state the recovery here rather than hide it. For scale: the year before, capital actuals were Rs 2,897 crore; the year after, Rs 4,533 crore.
caveats.source_publisher: AP Finance Department, Demands for Grants 2024-25, Volume III/7

caveats.title: A few totals do not add up, and that is the document's doing
caveats.body: In a handful of rows the printed total is a little larger than revenue plus capital. That is almost certainly a loans and advances line that sits in the demand but not in either column. We print what the document prints rather than silently correcting it.

schools.what_it_is: Total schools, enrolment and teachers in Andhra Pradesh as counted by UDISE+, the Ministry of Education's annual school census.

source.publisher: Ministry of Education, Government of India
source.name: UDISE+ / DISE

schools.coverage_warning: UDISE+ begins at 2018-19. For 2014-15 to 2017-18 the series was DISE, published by NIEPA, and no government-hosted copy could be found - the old udise.in host is no longer a government site. Those four years are shown as not found, never estimated. Enrolment is missing for 2018-19 to 2020-21 because those booklets place it in a chapter our reader could not reach.
schools.counting_note: This is a NET count. Schools were built and upgraded in these years, and schools were also merged and closed under school rationalisation. A fall in the total does not mean nothing was built, and a rise does not mean nothing was closed. Read it beside the construction orders, not instead of them.

reconciliation.why: Every figure here was checked against a second government source before publication. This section exists because an earlier version of this page was published without such a check and was wrong.

checks.check: Teachers, UDISE+ booklets against a Lok Sabha answer
checks.result: PASS - 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24 match exactly in both documents

checks.check: Enrolment 2023-24, UDISE+ NEP booklet against UDISE+ Existing-structure booklet
checks.result: PASS - identical state totals in both; the two structures differ only in the category split

checks.check: Government Order rupee sums against Demand XII
checks.result: EXPECTED SHORTFALL, and the reason GO amounts are never published as spending. Construction-section sanction orders come to roughly 22 per cent of Demand XII for TDP 2014-19, 19 per cent for YSRCP 2019-24 and 13 per cent for TDP 2024-. Only orders that happen to state a figure can be counted at all, so the sum is a floor of one kind of order, not departmental spending.

checks.check: CAG on the capital outlay spike in 2020-21 and 2021-22
checks.result: FLAGGED - the auditor found repairs, painting, desks and fans booked as capital expenditure under Mana Badi Nadu Nedu Phase I. The rise is real but partly an accounting choice the CAG objected to. Carried as a high-severity caveat on the chart.

extraction_defects_found_and_fixed: Rupee amounts written 'Rs.944.53 crores' were invisible to the first extraction, which only read 'Rs.9,37,63,92,000/-'. That dropped Rs 28,019 crore of YSRCP orders against Rs 955 crore of TDP 2014-19 orders. Both notations are now read.
The component pattern for digital classrooms matched 'ICT' inside the word DISTRICT, inflating it from 10 orders to 1,004. Fixed with word boundaries.

management_series.what_it_is: Schools, enrolment and teachers in Andhra Pradesh, split by who runs them, for ten years. This is the series that answers the question the earlier version of this page could not: whether government schools were built or closed, as opposed to a total that mixed government and private schools together and so could not tell the two apart.

source.publisher: Commissionerate of School Education, Government of Andhra Pradesh
source.name: Educational Statistics 2022-23, Tables 92, 93 and 94, printed pages 196 to 198
source.underlying: The volume names its own source as UDISE Plus data 2022-23.
source.why_this_table: Each annual volume also prints a management-wise table for its own year, but the definitions move between volumes: the 2019-20 and 2020-21 books add a higher-secondary-only column that the others do not. This single ten-year table is the state restating every year on one consistent basis, so it is the one used here. The seven individual volumes were extracted separately as a cross-check and agree with it.

management_series.government_definition: Government means Central Government plus State Government plus Local Bodies, added here from the table's own columns. Private Aided is shown separately because an aided school is privately run on public money, and folding it into either side would mislead.

caveats.title: The state changed what it counted twice, and says so
caveats.body: The volume's own notes record that from 2022-23 Private Unaided includes unrecognised schools and madarasas, and NCLP schools were moved into State Government. Both changes are small but they land in the last year of the series, so a reader comparing 2022-23 with 2013-14 is not comparing identical definitions.

caveats.title: Enrolment before 2016-17 is not comparable with what follows
caveats.body: The volume states that from 2016-17 enrolment counts classes I to X only. The first three years therefore sit on a wider definition and should not be read as part of the same trend line.

caveats.title: A drop of 1,752 local-body schools between 2014-15 and 2015-16 is unexplained
caveats.body: Local Bodies fall from 42,418 to 40,703 in a single year. The volume gives no reason. A change that large in one year is more likely to be a reorganisation or a change in what was counted than 1,752 school closures, and this platform does not attribute it to any government's action without a document that says so.

caveats.title: This is a different count from UDISE+ figures shown elsewhere
caveats.body: Other pages may cite UDISE+ totals directly. Those run higher because they include schools of departments outside School Education. The two series are kept apart and never plotted as one line.
